steps.description: We begin with the **public interface** of the `Transmuter`. The **interface** tells us the shape of positions, configuration parameters, **read-only getters**, **governance hooks**, **user flows**, and **emitted events**. Think of it as the contract’s `menu` – everything an external caller can rely on.

Two structs define the primary data handled by the Transmuter.
- lines 7-14 – StakingPosition records how much was staked and when it can be claimed.
- lines 16-23 – TransmuterInitializationParams bundles constructor inputs such as token addresses, fees, and the staking graph size.

Read-only view functions expose contract state:
- alchemist / admin / pendingAdmin (lines 25-38)
- version (40-42)
- syntheticToken, depositCap, exitFee, graphSize, transmutationFee, timeToTransmute, totalLocked (43-66)
- alchemists(index) – iterate registered alchemists (67-69)
- protocolFeeReceiver (70)

Governance-only mutators allow the admin to adjust settings:
- setPendingAdmin / acceptAdmin (72-93) – two-step admin transfer.
- setAlchemist (94-98) – redirect redemption source.
- setDepositCap, setTransmutationTime, setTransmutationFee, setExitFee (99-128) – risk knobs.
- setProtocolFeeReceiver (130-137) – where collected fees are sent.

Core user flows:
- getPosition (139-145) – inspect an NFT position.
- createRedemption (146-153) – lock synthetic tokens and mint NFT.
- claimRedemption (155-163) – burn NFT and receive underlying.
- queryGraph (165-171) – helper for off-chain accounting of pending redemptions.

Events broadcast state changes & user activity, enabling off-chain indexers to react:
- `AdminUpdated` / `PendingAdminUpdated` / `AlchemistUpdated`
- `PositionCreated` / `PositionClaimed`
- `GraphSizeUpdated`, `DepositCapUpdated`, `TransmutationTimeUpdated`, `TransmutationFeeUpdated`, `ExitFeeUpdated`, `ProtocolFeeReceiverUpdated`

Custom errors make reverts gas-efficient and self-describing.
Highlighted failure modes include:
- `NotRegisteredAlchemist` / `AlchemistDuplicateEntry`
- `DepositCapReached` / `DepositZeroAmount` / `DepositTooLarge`
- `PositionNotFound` / `PrematureClaim`
- `CallerNotOwner`

The implementation file links everything together.
lines 18-22 show the contract-level comment and the `contract Transmuter is ITransmuter, ERC721` declaration – confirming that the logic we’ll explore later faithfully implements the interface and represents each position as an **ERC-721 NFT**.
